summary: Interpreted the real-cluster receipt and integrated it into the parent account. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e parsed cleanly and all seven comparisons evaluated: the restarted node reports {A,B,C} instead of the committed {A,B,C,D,E} (violated, witness index 1), the stale-configured node reaches Leader holding two of five voters (violated, index 2), the cluster shows two leaders (violated, index 2), the two leaders commit different entries at the same index 11 in term 3 (violated, index 2), the minority leader commits an entry (violated, index 2), while the in-partition control node with the current configuration never leads and the rest of the cluster keeps reporting {A,B,C,D,E} (both hold, index 2). The child question therefore has an experiment-level violated/asserted interpretation and a question-level explained/asserted account; the parent question's interpretation was revised to replace its pending-election limitation with this confirmed split-brain witness, with joint_history explaining how the two receipts (supplied-store construction and live-cluster witness) belong to one behaviour chain, and the quorum fact gained the new receipt as a recorded execution. Limits now recorded: no no-feature restart control inside the cluster, graceful shutdown instead of a crash, in-memory stores and a transport-only partition over one window, unobserved post-healing fate of the conflicting entry, and stale-membership persistence still argued from the AppendEntries duplicate-skip rather than observed over a long window. Incomplete: a healing-phase successor experiment to observe whether the same-index/same-term divergent entries survive unrepairable, and the earlier registered constructor replay-backpressure question.
